facts: Cory Doctorow's *Little Brother* was released by Project Gutenberg on September 30, 2009.
The novel was written in eight weeks from May to July 2007.
*Little Brother* received endorsements from authors Neil Gaiman and John Scalzi.
The book is dedicated to independent bookstores in each chapter.
Marcus Yallow is accused of hacking the school's security systems.
Vice Principal Benson lacks concrete evidence against Marcus.
Marcus and Darryl skip school to participate in Harajuku Fun Madness.
Darryl's library book contains an RFID tag that allows the school to track students.
Marcus and his friends disable a library book's RFID tag in the school microwave.
Marcus uses a botnet to disable a bully's phone named Charles.
The group participates in an alternate reality game called Harajuku Fun Madness.
A massive earthquake strikes San Francisco during a confrontation with a rival team.
Marcus and three friends are abducted by unmarked military personnel at Powell Street BART station.
Marcus is interrogated by Department of Homeland Security agents about suspicious devices found on him.
Marcus demands to know if he's under arrest and requests an attorney during his interrogation.
A female agent threatens Marcus with disappearance if he does not unlock his phone and decrypt its files.
Marcus is detained and interrogated by government agents following a terrorist attack.
His interrogator is referred to as "Severe Haircut Lady."
Marcus is coerced into signing documents that falsely declare his detention voluntary.
He is released onto a city street after being hooded and transported by ship.
The protagonist reunites with friends Vanessa and Jolu after being released from illegal detention.
The protagonist learns that terrorist attacks on the Bay Bridge and BART have killed thousands.
The protagonist discovers a keystroke-logging bug in his custom laptop.
He builds a ParanoidXbox to provide anonymous, secure internet access.
Marcus is a 17-year-old activist in San Francisco.
He runs an underground digital resistance movement called the Xnet.
Marcus is pursued by suspected DHS agents.
He surrenders to SFPD detectives at a local restaurant.
Marcus created the secret Xnet encrypted network in San Francisco.
Jolu works at the independent ISP Pigspleen Net.
Marcus apologizes to Jolu and they reconcile.
Vanessa abandons the group due to fear of the risks involved.
The Department of Homeland Security employs pervasive monitoring systems in post-9/11 San Francisco.
Marcus launches "Operation False Positive" on his Xnet to teach others to use RFID cloners.
The operation causes widespread chaos, including clogged traffic and airport delays.
Marcus's father, a surveillance proponent, is pulled over multiple times in a single day.
Marcus is a San Francisco teenager involved with the Xnet.
The Department of Homeland Security received a 300% budget increase.
Marcus and his friend Jolu establish a secure communication system using cryptographic web of trust technology.
Marcus's father Drew shifts from criticizing to supporting invasive surveillance tactics.
Marcus and Jolu organize a secret keysigning party at Sutro Baths in San Francisco.
Jolu quits the keysigning party due to fear and surveillance risks faced by people of color.
Marcus uses a specially-built ParanoidLinux laptop to help participants generate cryptographic key-pairs.
Participants verify their public keys by photographing them and manually typing them into their computers.
The protagonist and Jolu organize a secretive beach gathering to join Xnet.
The narrator experienced DHS detention following a bombing.
Ange's slogan "Don't Trust Anyone Over 25" becomes popular during the gathering.
Ms. Galvez discusses the 1960s Yippies' Vietnam War protests in class.
Marcus attends a classroom discussion about the Declaration of Independence.
Marcus goes on a date with Ange at an illegal rave in Dolores Park.
Militarized police deploy 1.5 million Scovilles of pepper spray into the crowd.
Ms. Galvez is removed from class and replaced with a DHS-approved curriculum.
Marcus is the teenage activist behind the online persona M1k3y.
He documents a violently suppressed protest in Dolores Park through a comprehensive website.
Major news outlets like Al-Jazeera and NPR broadcast the Xnet's coverage.
School authorities respond with authoritarian measures, including suspensions and threats of arrest.
Marcus was suspended from school for criticizing the DHS.
Marcus posted a video of DHS agents restraining General Claude Geist to his Xnet blog.
The video led to the creation of the "AbusesOfAuthority" movement.
Marcus held a masked press conference in the virtual world Clockwork Plunder.
Marcus orchestrates a press conference in an online game to expose the DHS's surveillance.
The media misrepresents Marcus's message as support for terrorism.
Darryl has been imprisoned at a secret DHS detention facility on Treasure Island for three months.
Marcus confesses his own arrest and imprisonment to his mother.
Marcus Yallow was illegally detained by the DHS.
Marcus founded the Xnet resistance network.
Marcus revealed he is M1k3y, the leader of Xnet.
Barbara Stratford agreed to publish the complete story about Xnet.
Marcus meets with journalist Barbara to expose Xnet.
Masha claims to be a DHS infiltrator warning Marcus of his imminent arrest.
Masha provides video evidence of DHS officials discussing plans to manipulate the midterms.
Marcus and Ange agree to work with Masha in exchange for a major Xnet distraction.
The author fabricated a story about a fictional "Old People" cult for an Italian travel magazine editor.
The hoax about the "Old People" cult was published and spread to major outlets including the New York Times.
Marcus introduces his girlfriend Ange to his parents, Lillian and Drew.
Ange gifts Lillian a spare hot-sauce mister before departing.

The narrator organizes a mass urban game called VampMob in San Francisco. Over 1,000 participants play tag during the VampMob event. Masha, a former acquaintance, detains the narrator at gunpoint. The narrator steals Masha's phone containing a photograph of his friend Darryl before escaping.
Marcus is a fugitive activist evading capture after the Bay Bridge bombing.
He entrusts Masha's phone to Van, containing incriminating video evidence.
Marcus is captured by Department of Homeland Security agents and taken to a detention facility on Treasure Island.
California Highway Patrol officers raid the facility and rescue Marcus from torture.
Marcus Yallow is a 17-year-old torture survivor.
Carrie Johnstone was cleared by a military tribunal and returned to active duty.
Marcus Yallow and Ange launched a political campaign called the "Coalition of Voters for a Free America."
Marcus is working with the ACLU on a civil lawsuit against the DHS.
